question: On 8 July 2026, the European Parliament approved the Protocol amending the EuroMediterranean Aviation Agreement between the European Community and its Member States, of the one part, and the Kingdom of Morocco, of the other part (EU-Morocco aviation agreement), to take account of the accession of Croatia. The agreement does not cover the separate and distinct territory of Western Sahara.

However, European airlines are currently operating the Paris-Dajla route, on Transavia, Madrid-Dajla, on Ryanair, and Las Palmas de Gran Canaria-El Aaiún, on Binter. As these connections are not covered by the EU-Morocco aviation agreement: 1.
What is the legal and administrative basis for operating the mentioned routes and which bilateral agreements or national authorisations cover them?
Have France and Spain informed the Commission of these agreements or authorisations, in accordance with Regulation (EC) No 847/2004?

Has the Commission assessed their compatibility with EU law and, in particular, with the judgments of the Court of Justice of 4 October 2024, which confirm the separate and distinct status of Western Sahara and the need for the consent of the Sahrawi people in order for an international agreement to apply to that territory?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (2.9.2026) As rightly pointed out by the Honourable Member, in accordance with the case law of the Court of Justice, the Euro-Mediterranean aviation agreement between the EU and Morocco does not apply to routes from the territory of an EU Member State to the territory of the Western Sahara.

The legal basis for operating the mentioned routes is established by the bilateral agreements concluded by the Member States from whose territories these routes are operated. The bilateral agreements concerned have been notified under Regulation (EC) No 847/20041. The agreement between France and Morocco was concluded in 1957 and was notified to the Commission on 23 September 2004.

The agreement between Spain and Morocco was concluded in 1970 and was notified to the Commission on 16 July 2004. The Commission assessed their compatibility with EU law as established in Regulation (EC) No 847/2004.
